ajmer|Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra.title: Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra

ajmer|Ajmer Sharif Dargah.description: Sufi tomb of Moinuddin Chishti at Ajmer
ajmer|Ajmer Sharif Dargah.extract: The Shrine of Mu'in al-Din Chishti, also known as the Ajmer Dargah Shareef, is a Sufi dargah complex incorporating the shrine of Mu'in al-Din Chishti, several tombs, and a mosque, located at Ajmer, in the state of Rajasthan, India. amritsar|Partition Museum.title: Partition Museum

aurangabad|Ajanta Caves.title: Ajanta Caves

haridwar|Har Ki Pauri.extract:
Har Ki Pauri is a sacred ghat on the banks of the Ganges River in the Hindu holy city of Haridwar, in the Indian state of Uttarakhand.

Laad Bazaar (urdu: لاڈ بازار) or Churi Bazaar is a market located in Hyderabad, India on one of the four main roads that branch out from the Charminar.

hyderabad|Qutb Shahi Tombs.description: Historical Islamic tomb in Hyderabad, Telangana, India
hyderabad|Qutb Shahi Tombs.extract:
The Qutub Shahi tombs are a series of Islamic tombs and mosques built by the various kings of the Qutub Shahi dynasty, located in the Ibrahim Bagh (garden precinct), close to the famous Golconda Fort in Hyderabad, in the Hyderabad district of the state of Telangana, India.

hyderabad|Salar Jung Museum.name: Salar Jung Museum
hyderabad|Salar Jung Museum.title: Salar Jung Museum

leh|Thiksey Monastery.extract: Thiksey Monastery or Thiksey Gompa (also transliterated from Ladakhi as Thikse, Thiksay or Tikse) is a Buddhist monastery affiliated with the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism. It is located on top of a hill in Thiksey approximately 19 kilometres (12 mi) east of Leh, in the Ladakh region of northern India.
leh|Thiksey Monastery.name: Thiksey Monastery
leh|Thiksey Monastery.title: Thikse Monastery

madurai|Alagar Koyil.description: Perumal temple in Madurai district, Tamil Nadu, India
madurai|Alagar Koyil.extract: Kallalagar Temple or Kallazhagar Temple, also known by its own toponym Thirumaliruncholai, is a Hindu temple dedicated to the protector god Vishnu in Alagar Koyil, a village in Madurai district in the South Indian state of Tamil Nadu. Constructed in the Tamil Style of Architecture, the temple is glorified in the Naalayira Divya Prabandham, the early medieval Tamil canon of the Azhvar saints from the 6th–9th centuries CE. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams dedicated to Vishnu, who is worshiped as Kallalagar, and his consort Lakshmi as Thirumagal.
madurai|Alagar Koyil.name: Alagar Koyil
madurai|Alagar Koyil.title: Kallalagar Temple

madurai|Gandhi Memorial Museum.description: Memorial museum , Biographical museum in Madurai, India
madurai|Gandhi Memorial Museum.extract: Gandhi Memorial Museum, established in 1959, is a memorial museum for Mahatma Gandhi located in the city of Madurai in Tamil Nadu, India. Known as Gandhi Museum, it is now one of the five Gandhi Sanghralayas (Gandhi Museums) in the country.
madurai|Gandhi Memorial Museum.name: Gandhi Memorial Museum
madurai|Gandhi Memorial Museum.title: Gandhi Memorial Museum, Madurai

madurai|Meenakshi Amman Temple.description: Historic Hindu temple in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, India
madurai|Meenakshi Amman Temple.extract: Meenakshi Temple, also known as Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple, is a historic Hindu temple located on the southern bank of the Vaigai River in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, India. It is dedicated to Meenakshi, a form of Parvati, and her consort Sundareswarar (Shiva).

madurai|Thirumalai Nayakkar Mahal.extract: Thirumalai Nayakkar Mahal is a palace located 2 km (1.2 mi) to the southeast of the Meenakshi Amman Temple in central Madurai, Tamil Nadu, India. It was built by Tirumala Nayaka, a king of the Madurai Nayak dynasty who ruled Madurai from 1623 to 1659, and was completed in 1636.

madurai|Vandiyur Mariamman Teppakulam.extract: Vandiyur Mariamman Temple is a Hindu Temple in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, India. It is dedicated to Mariamman.

madurai|Vandiyur Mariamman Teppakulam.title: Vandiyur Mariamman Temple

madurai|Vishaal Mall.description: Shopping mall in Tamil Nadu, India
madurai|Vishaal Mall.extract: Vishaal Mall is a shopping mall in the city of Madurai, Tamil Nadu. It is the 20th large format mall in southern Tamil Nadu and the city's first integrated multi-utility mall.
madurai|Vishaal Mall.name: Vishaal Mall
madurai|Vishaal Mall.title: Vishaal Mall

manali|Atal Tunnel.extract: Atal Tunnel (Hindi: अटल सुरंग)  is a 9.02-kilometre-long (5.60 mi) road tunnel connecting Manali and Keylong, thus helping in bypassing the Rohtang Pass, Himachal Pradesh in the eastern Pir Panjal range of the Himalayas. It carries two lanes of National Highway 3 and is the longest highway single-tube tunnel above 10,000 feet (3,048 m) in the world.
manali|Atal Tunnel.name: Atal Tunnel
manali|Atal Tunnel.title: Atal Tunnel

manali|Hadimba Devi Temple.description: Hindu temple in Himachal Pradesh, India
manali|Hadimba Devi Temple.extract: Hidimba Devi Temple, locally known as Dhungari Temple, also known variously as the Hadimba Temple, is a Hindu Temple, located in Manāli, a hill station in the State of Himāchal Pradesh in north India. It is an ancient cave temple dedicated to Hidimbi Devi, wife of Bhima, a figure in the Indian epic Mahābhārata.
manali|Hadimba Devi Temple.name: Hadimba Devi Temple
manali|Hadimba Devi Temple.title: Hidimba Devi Temple

manali|Rohtang Pass.extract: Rohtang Pass  (Rohtang, literally meaning "pile of corpses") is a high mountain pass (elevation 3,980 m (13,058 ft)) on the eastern end of the Pir Panjal Range of the Himalayas around 51 km (32 mi) from Manali in the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh, It connects the Kullu Valley with the Lahaul and Spiti Valleys of Himachal Pradesh, India.
manali|Rohtang Pass.name: Rohtang Pass
manali|Rohtang Pass.title: Rohtang Pass

manali|Solang Valley.extract: Solang Valley derives its name from a combination of the words Solang (Nearby village) and Nallah (water stream). It is a side valley at the top of the Kullu Valley in Himachal Pradesh, India 14 km northwest of the resort town Manali on the way to Rohtang Pass, and is known for its summer and winter sports conditions.
manali|Solang Valley.name: Solang Valley
manali|Solang Valley.title: Solang Valley

manali|Vashisht Hot Springs.extract: Vashisht is a village in Kullu district, Himachal Pradesh, India. It is a popular tourist place.
manali|Vashisht Hot Springs.name: Vashisht Hot Springs
manali|Vashisht Hot Springs.title: Vashisht, Himachal Pradesh

mathura|Dwarkadhish Temple.description: Radha Dwarkadhish Temple in Mathura, Uttar Pradesh
mathura|Dwarkadhish Temple.extract: Shri Dwarkadhish Temple is a Hindu temple in Mathura, Uttar Pradesh, India. In this historic temple, Krishna is worshipped in his Dwarkanath or Dwarkadhish form along with his feminine counterpart goddess Radha in the form of Radharani.
mathura|Dwarkadhish Temple.name: Dwarkadhish Temple
mathura|Dwarkadhish Temple.title: Dwarkadhish Temple, Mathura

mathura|Government Museum Mathura.extract: Government Museum, Mathura, commonly referred to as Mathura museum, is an archaeological museum in Mathura city of Uttar Pradesh state in India. The museum was founded by then collector of the Mathura district, Sir F. S. Growse in 1874.
mathura|Government Museum Mathura.name: Government Museum Mathura
mathura|Government Museum Mathura.title: Government Museum, Mathura

mathura|Kusum Sarovar.description: Historic and sacred site in Vrindavan, Uttar Pradesh
mathura|Kusum Sarovar.extract: Kusum Sarovar is considered in Hinduism a sacred water reservoir with a historic sand monument in its backdrop. It is situated on the holy Govardhan Hill between Manasi Ganga and Radha Kund in Mathura district of Uttar Pradesh, India.
mathura|Kusum Sarovar.name: Kusum Sarovar
mathura|Kusum Sarovar.title: Kusum Sarovar

mathura|Shri Krishna Janmasthan.description: Birth place of Hindu god Krishna in Mathura, India
mathura|Shri Krishna Janmasthan.extract: Krishna Janmasthan Temple is a Hindu temple situated in Mathura, Uttar Pradesh, India. There are three main temples inside the premises -- Keshavdev temple which is dedicated to Krishna, Garbh Griha where Krishna is believed to be born in Dvapar Yuga and Bhagvata Bhavan where presiding deities are Radha Krishna.
mathura|Shri Krishna Janmasthan.name: Shri Krishna Janmasthan
mathura|Shri Krishna Janmasthan.title: Krishna Janmasthan Temple Complex

mathura|Vishram Ghat.extract: Vishram Ghat is a ghat, a bath and worship place, on the banks of river Yamuna in Mathura, India. The traditional parikrama starts and ends at Vishram Ghat.
mathura|Vishram Ghat.name: Vishram Ghat
mathura|Vishram Ghat.title: Vishram Ghat

mumbai|Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Termi.description: Historic terminal train station in Mumbai, India
mumbai|Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Termi.extract:
Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (CST), officially Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) and also known as Victoria Terminus (VT), is a historic railway terminus and UNESCO World Heritage Site in Mumbai (Bombay), Maharashtra, India.
The terminus was designed by a British architectural engineer Frederick William Stevens from an initial design by Axel Haig, in an exuberant Indo Gothic style.

mumbai|Colaba Causeway.description: Neighbourhood in Mumbai City, Maharashtra, India
mumbai|Colaba Causeway.extract:
Colaba Causeway, officially known as Shahid Bhagat Singh Road, is a commercial street, and a major causeway or land link between Colaba and the Old Woman's Island in the city of Mumbai, India.
It lies close to the Fort area, and to the east of Cuffe Parade, an upmarket neighbourhood in South Mumbai, and close by are Mumbai's famous landmarks, the Gateway of India and Taj Mahal Palace & Tower.
mumbai|Colaba Causeway.name: Colaba Causeway
mumbai|Colaba Causeway.title: Colaba Causeway

mumbai|Crawford Market.extract: Crawford Market (officially the Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Mandai) is one of South Mumbai's most famous markets. The building was completed in 1869, and donated to the city by Cowasji Jehangir.
mumbai|Crawford Market.name: Crawford Market
mumbai|Crawford Market.title: Crawford Market

mumbai|Elephanta Caves.description: Collection of cave temples in Maharashtra, India
mumbai|Elephanta Caves.extract: The Elephanta Caves form a collection of cave temples predominantly dedicated to the Hindu god Shiva; UNESCO has designated them as a World Heritage Site. They are located on Elephanta Island, or Gharapuri (literally meaning "the city of the caves"), in Mumbai Harbour, 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) east of Mumbai in the Indian state of Maharashtra.
mumbai|Elephanta Caves.name: Elephanta Caves
mumbai|Elephanta Caves.title: Elephanta Caves

mumbai|Gateway of India.extract: The Gateway of India is an arch-monument, completed in 1924, on the waterfront of Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. It was erected to commemorate the landing of King George V of the United Kingdom for his coronation as the Emperor of India in December 1911 at Strand Road near Wellington Fountain.

mumbai|Leopold Cafe.extract: The Leopold Cafe and Bar is a restaurant and bar on Colaba Causeway, Colaba, Mumbai, India, located across from the Colaba Police station. It was one of the first sites attacked in the 2008 Mumbai attacks.
mumbai|Leopold Cafe.name: Leopold Cafe
mumbai|Leopold Cafe.title: Leopold Cafe

mumbai|Marine Drive.extract: Marine Drive, often referred to as the Queen's Necklace, is a 3-kilometre-long promenade along the Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Road in Mumbai (Bombay), India. The road and promenade were constructed by Pallonji Mistry in 1940.
mumbai|Marine Drive.name: Marine Drive
mumbai|Marine Drive.title: Marine Drive, Mumbai

mumbai|R City Mall.extract: R City Mall is a shopping mall located in Ghatkopar West, Mumbai. The mall spreads across 1.2 million square feet with the capacity to house over 350 stores.

mumbai|Siddhivinayak Temple.extract: The Shri Siddhivinayak Ganapati Mandir is a Hindu temple dedicated to Ganesha.  It is located in Prabhadevi neighbourhood of Mumbai, Maharashtra.
mumbai|Siddhivinayak Temple.name: Siddhivinayak Temple
mumbai|Siddhivinayak Temple.title: Siddhivinayak Temple, Mumbai

munnar|Mattupetty Dam.description: Dam in the mountains of Kerala, India
munnar|Mattupetty Dam.extract: Mattupetty Dam (Madupetty Dam), Kannan Devan Hills in Idukki District,  is a  storage concrete gravity dam built  in  the mountains of Kerala, India, to conserve water for hydroelectricity. It has been a vital source of power and huge revenue for Idukki District.

mussoorie|Kempty Falls.description: Waterfall in Ram Gaon, Uttarakhand, India
mussoorie|Kempty Falls.extract: Kempty Falls is a waterfall in Ram Gaon and at the south of Kempty, in the Tehri Garhwal District of Uttarakhand, India. It is 13 kilometres (8 mi) from Mussoorie on the Chakrata Road, and 45 kilometres (28 mi) from Dehradun.

mysuru|Brindavan Gardens.extract: The Brindavan Gardens is a garden located 12 k.ms from the city of Mysore in the Mandya District of the Indian State of Karnataka. It lies adjoining the Krishnarajasagara Dam which is built across the river Kaveri.

mysuru|Chamundi Hill (Chamundeshwari Tem.extract: The Chamundeshwari Temple is a Hindu temple located on the top of Chamundi Hills about 13 km from the palace city of Mysuru in the state of Karnataka in India. The temple was named after Chamundeshwari or, the fierce form of Shakti, a tutelary deity held in reverence for centuries by the Maharaja of Mysuru.

mysuru|Devaraja Market.description: Market in Mysore in Karnataka, India
mysuru|Devaraja Market.extract: Devaraja Market is a market located in Mysuru, India. One can buy flowers, fruits, and choose from conical piles of colorful Kumkum powder.

mysuru|Devaraja Market.title: Devaraja Market

mysuru|Mall of Mysore.extract: Mall of Mysore is a shopping mall which is one of the largest and the first of its kind in the Indian city of Mysore, Karnataka. It is located next to the Mysore Racecourse, with the Chamundi hills as a backdrop.

mysuru|Mysore Palace.description: Historical palace in Mysore, Karnataka, India
mysuru|Mysore Palace.extract: Mysore Palace, also known as Amba Vilas Palace, is a historic palace and royal residence located in Mysore, Karnataka, India. It served as the official residence of the Wadiyar dynasty and the seat of the Kingdom of Mysore, and was commissioned by Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV in August 1897 following the destruction of the previous structure in a fire.
mysuru|Mysore Palace.name: Mysore Palace
mysuru|Mysore Palace.title: Mysore Palace

mysuru|Mysuru Zoo.extract: Mysore Zoo (or Mysuru Zoo), officially known as Sri Chamarajendra Zoological Gardens, is a composite of zoological gardens and animal park located in the southern Indian city of Mysore, Karnataka. Stretching across a 157-acre (64 ha)-expanse and situated at about 700 metres (0.43 miles) from Mysore Palace, it is the oldest zoo in India and one of the oldest in the world.
mysuru|Mysuru Zoo.name: Mysuru Zoo
mysuru|Mysuru Zoo.title: Mysore Zoo

mysuru|Sayyaji Rao Road.extract: Sayyajirao Road, also known as Sayyaji Rao Road, is a road in Mysore, India stretching in the north from Agrahara circle at one end to Highway circle at the other. This road was named after Maharaja Sayajirao Gaekwad by Maharaja Chamaraja Wodayar X in 1893.

nainital|Naini Lake.extract: Naini Tal, also known as Naini Lake, is a natural freshwater body, situated amidst the town of Nainital in Kumaon, Uttarakhand, India. It is tectonic in origin and was almost circular, until frequent landslides made it crescent shaped and has an outfall at the southeastern end.

ooty|Government Botanical Garden.description: Botanical garden in Tamil Nadu, India
ooty|Government Botanical Garden.extract: The Government Botanical Garden is a botanical garden in Udhagamandalam, near Coimbatore (Ooty), Tamil Nadu state, India laid out in 1848. The gardens, divided into several sections, cover an area of around 22 hectares (54 acres), and lie on the lower slopes of Doddabetta peak.

ooty|Government Botanical Garden.title: Government Botanical Garden

ooty|Government Rose Garden.description: Rose garden in Ooty, Tamil Nadu, India
ooty|Government Rose Garden.extract: The Government Rose Garden (formerly known as the Jayalalithaa Rose Garden, Centenary Rose Park and Nootrandu Roja Poonga) is situated on the slopes of Elk Hill in Vijayanagaram of Ooty town in Tamil Nadu, India at an altitude of 2200 meters.

ooty|Government Rose Garden.title: Government Rose Garden

ooty|Ooty Lake.description: Artificial lake in Tamil Nadu, India
ooty|Ooty Lake.extract: Ooty lake is an artificial lake near Ooty in the Nilgiris district of Tamil Nadu, India. It covers an area of 26 hectares (64 acres).

ooty|Ooty Lake.title: Ooty Lake

ooty|Ooty Municipal Market.description: Retail market in Tamil Nadu, India
ooty|Ooty Municipal Market.extract: The Ooty Municipal Market is located in the Nilgiris district in Tamil Nadu. Built in 1848, it was previously considered to be a model market in India.

ooty|Ooty Municipal Market.title: Ooty Municipal Market

pondicherry|Auroville (Matrimandir).description: Spiritual building in Tamil Nadu, India
pondicherry|Auroville (Matrimandir).extract: The Matrimandir is an edifice of spiritual significance for practitioners of integral yoga in the centre of Auroville, India established by Mirra Alfassa of the Sri Aurobindo Ashram,  Auroville's spiritual co-founder, known to her followers as The Mother or La Mère. It is called Soul of the City (French: L'âme de la Ville) and situated in a large open space called "Paix" (French for Peace).

pondicherry|Auroville (Matrimandir).title: Matrimandir

pondicherry|Basilica of the Sacred Heart.extract: Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus (Tamil: பரிசுத்த இருதய ஆண்டவர் தேவாலயம், French: Basilique du Sacré-Cœur de Jésus de Pondichéry) is a Roman Catholic minor basilica situated on the south boulevard of Pondicherry in Puducherry, India, and is an oriental specimen of Gothic Revival architecture. It contains rare stained glass panels depicting events from the life of Christ and saints of the Catholic Church.

prayagraj|Akshayavat.extract: Akshayavata (Sanskrit: अक्षयवट, romanized: Akṣayavaṭa, lit. 'undecaying banyan'), also rendered Akshayavat, is a sacred banyan tree mentioned in the Hindu mythology and in Jainism. It is also the name of a sacred lake mentioned in the Puranas.

prayagraj|All Saints Cathedral.extract:
All Saints' Cathedral, also known as Patthar Girja (Church of Stones), is a cathedral of the Church of North India located in Prayagraj, India.

prayagraj|Allahabad Fort.description: Fort in Allahabad, Uttar Pradesh, India
prayagraj|Allahabad Fort.extract: Allahabad Fort was built by the Mughal emperor Akbar at Allahabad (modern Prayagraj) in 1583. The fort stands on the banks of the Yamuna, near its confluence with the Ganges.

prayagraj|Anand Bhavan.description: Historic house museum in Prayagraj, India
prayagraj|Anand Bhavan.extract: Anand Bhavan (lit. 'abode of happiness') is a historic house museum in Prayagraj, India, focusing on the Nehru family. It was bought by Indian political leader Motilal Nehru in the 1930s to serve as the residence of the Nehru family when the original mansion Swaraj Bhavan (previously called Anand Bhavan) was transformed into the local headquarters of the Indian National Congress.

prayagraj|Khusro Bagh.extract: Bagh-e-Khusrau is a large walled garden and burial complex located in muhalla Khuldabad, close to the Prayagraj Junction railway station, in Allahabad, India. It is roughly 6 km from the Akbari fort at Sangam (built-in r.

prayagraj|Triveni Sangam.description: Junction of three rivers in India
prayagraj|Triveni Sangam.extract: In Hindu tradition, Triveni Sangam is a confluence (Sanskrit: sangama) of three rivers that is a sacred place, with a bath there said to flush away all of one's sins and free one from the cycle of rebirth. puri|Gundicha Temple.description: Hindu temple in Puri, Odisha, India
puri|Gundicha Temple.extract: Gundicha Temple  (Odia: ଗୁଣ୍ଡିଚା ମନ୍ଦିର), is a Hindu temple, situated in the temple town of Puri in the state of Odisha, India. It is significant for being the destination of the celebrated annual Rath Yatra of Puri.

puri|Jagannath Temple.description: Hindu temple at Puri, Odisha, India
puri|Jagannath Temple.extract: The Jagannath Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to Jagannath, a form of Vishnu. It is located in Puri, Odisha, on the eastern coast of India.

puri|Jagannath Temple.title: Jagannath Temple, Puri

puri|Puri Beach.extract: Puri Beach or the Golden beach is a beach in the city of Puri in the state of Odisha, India. It is on the shore of the Bay of Bengal.

puri|Puri Beach.title: Puri Beach

puri|Raghurajpur Artist Village.extract: Raghurajpur is a heritage crafts village in Puri district, Odisha, India, known for its master Pattachitra painters, an art form which dates back to 5 BC in the region, and Gotipua dance troupes, the precursor to the Indian classical dance form of Odissi. It is also known as the birthplace of the Odissi exponents Padma Vibhushan Guru and Kelucharan Mohapatra and the Gotipua dancer Padma Shri Guru Maguni Charan Das.
puri|Raghurajpur Artist Village.name: Raghurajpur Artist Village
puri|Raghurajpur Artist Village.title: Raghurajpur

pushkar|Brahma Temple.description: Hindu temple dedicated to Brahma in Rajasthan, India
pushkar|Brahma Temple.extract:
Brahma Temple, Pushkar (also known as Jagatpita Brahma Mandir) is a Hindu temple situated at Pushkar in the Indian state of Rajasthan, close to the sacred Pushkar Lake to which its legend has an indelible link.
The temple is one of very few existing temples dedicated to the Hindu creator-god Brahma in India and remains the most prominent among them.The temple structure dates to the 14th century CE, with later partial rebuilding.
pushkar|Brahma Temple.name: Brahma Temple
pushkar|Brahma Temple.title: Brahma Temple, Pushkar

pushkar|Pushkar Lake.extract: Pushkar Lake or Pushkar Sarovar is located in the town of Pushkar near Ajmer city in Ajmer district of the Rajasthan state of western India. Pushkar Lake is a sacred lake for the Hindus.
pushkar|Pushkar Lake.name: Pushkar Lake
pushkar|Pushkar Lake.title: Pushkar Lake

pushkar|Savitri Temple.extract: Savitri Mata Mandir or Savitri Temple is a Hindu temple of Goddess Savitri located in Ratnagiri hill which is a popular pilgrimage site in Pushkar, Ajmer district, Rajasthan, India. Savitri Mata Mandir is a hilltop Hindu temple.
pushkar|Savitri Temple.name: Savitri Temple
pushkar|Savitri Temple.title: Savitri Mata Mandir

rameswaram|Agni Theertham.description: Hindu pilgrimage site in Tamil Nadu, India
rameswaram|Agni Theertham.extract: Agni Tirtham is one of the Tirthas of Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu, India. The beach east of Ramanathaswamy Temple is known by this name.
rameswaram|Agni Theertham.name: Agni Theertham
rameswaram|Agni Theertham.title: Agni Tirtham

rameswaram|Dhanushkodi.description: Former town in Tamil Nadu, India
rameswaram|Dhanushkodi.extract: Dhanushkodi is an abandoned town at the south-eastern tip of Pamban Island of the state of Tamil Nadu in India. It is south-east of Pamban and is about 24 kilometres (15 mi) west of Talaimannar in Sri Lanka.
rameswaram|Dhanushkodi.name: Dhanushkodi
rameswaram|Dhanushkodi.title: Dhanushkodi

rameswaram|Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Memo.description: Memorial dedicated to A. P. J. Abdul Kalam in Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu, India
rameswaram|Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Memo.extract: Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Memorial is a memorial dedicated to the former president of the Republic of India A. P. J. Abdul Kalam located in Peikarumbu, Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu, India.
rameswaram|Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Memo.name: Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Memorial
rameswaram|Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Memo.osm_query: A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Memorial, Rameswaram
rameswaram|Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Memo.title: Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Memorial

rameswaram|Pamban Bridge.description: Railway bridge connecting Pamban Island to mainland India
rameswaram|Pamban Bridge.extract: Pamban Bridge (Tamil: [paːmbɐn], romanised: pāmban) was a railway bridge that connected the town of Rameswaram on Pamban Island with Mandapam in mainland India. Opened on 24 February 1914, it was India's first sea bridge, and was the longest sea bridge in India until the opening of the Bandra–Worli Sea Link in 2010.
rameswaram|Pamban Bridge.name: Pamban Bridge
rameswaram|Pamban Bridge.title: Pamban Bridge

rameswaram|Ramanathaswamy Temple.description: Hindu temple in Rameswaram island in the state of Tamil Nadu, India
rameswaram|Ramanathaswamy Temple.extract: Ramanathaswamy Temple (Rāmanātasvāmi Kōyil) is a Hindu temple dedicated to the Hindu god Shiva located on Rameswaram island in the state of Tamil Nadu, India. It is one of the twelve Jyotirlinga temples.
rameswaram|Ramanathaswamy Temple.name: Ramanathaswamy Temple

rishikesh|Beatles Ashram.extract: Beatles Ashram (बीटल्स आश्रम), also known as Chaurasi Kutia (चौरासी कुटिया), is an ashram close to the north Indian city of Rishikesh in the state of Uttarakhand. It is located on the eastern bank of the Ganges river, opposite the Muni Ki Reti area of Rishikesh, in the foothills of the Himalayas.
rishikesh|Beatles Ashram.name: Beatles Ashram
rishikesh|Beatles Ashram.title: Beatles Ashram

rishikesh|Lakshman Jhula.description: Footbridge across the Ganges in Uttarakhand, India
rishikesh|Lakshman Jhula.extract: Lakshman Jhula is a historic suspension bridge across the river Ganges, located northeast of Rishikesh in Uttarakhand, India. The bridge connects the village of Tapovan with Jonk and has been closed to traffic since 2020 due to safety concerns.
rishikesh|Lakshman Jhula.name: Lakshman Jhula
rishikesh|Lakshman Jhula.title: Lakshman Jhula

rishikesh|Neelkanth Mahadev Temple.extract: Neelkanth Mahadev Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to Nilkanth, an aspect of Shiva. Located approximately 32 km from Rishikesh in the Pauri Garhwal district of Uttarakhand, India, the temple is constructed in the Dravidian architectural style.
rishikesh|Neelkanth Mahadev Temple.name: Neelkanth Mahadev Temple
rishikesh|Neelkanth Mahadev Temple.title: Nilkanth Mahadev

rishikesh|Parmarth Niketan.extract: Parmarth Niketan is an ashram located in Rishikesh, Uttarakhand, India.
rishikesh|Parmarth Niketan.name: Parmarth Niketan
rishikesh|Parmarth Niketan.title: Parmarth Niketan

rishikesh|Ram Jhula.extract: Ram Jhula (Hindi: राम झूला) is an iron suspension bridge across the river Ganges, located 3 kilometres (1.9 mi) northeast of the city of Rishikesh in Uttarakhand, India. The bridge connects the Sivananda Nagar area of Muni Ki Reti in Tehri Garhwal district to the Swargashram area in Pauri Garhwal district, crossing the river from west to east.
rishikesh|Ram Jhula.name: Ram Jhula
rishikesh|Ram Jhula.title: Ram Jhula

rishikesh|Triveni Ghat.extract:
Triveni Ghat is the largest and most famous ghat in Rishikesh, Uttarakhand, situated on the banks of the Ganges.
Devotees visit the ghat to take ritual baths, believing it cleanses them of their sins.
rishikesh|Triveni Ghat.name: Triveni Ghat
rishikesh|Triveni Ghat.title: Triveni Ghat

sabarimala|Sabarimala Ayyappa Temple.extract: The Sabarimala Sree Dharma Sastha Temple (Malayalam: ശബരിമല ശ്രീ ധർമ്മ ശാസ്താ ക്ഷേത്രം) (Malayalam pronunciation: [ʃabəɾimala]) is a Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Sree Dharma Sastha where the deity is worshipped as Lord Ayyappan, an eternal brahmachari, the son of the deities Shiva and Mohini (female avatar of the god Vishnu), and is situated atop the Sabarimala hill in Pathanamthitta district of Kerala, India. The temple is surrounded by 18 hills in the Periyar Tiger Reserve.
sabarimala|Sabarimala Ayyappa Temple.name: Sabarimala Ayyappa Temple
sabarimala|Sabarimala Ayyappa Temple.title: Sabarimala Temple

shimla|Christ Church.extract: Christ Church, Shimla, is the second oldest church in North India, after St John's Church in Meerut.  Worship is conducted in Hindi and English.
shimla|Christ Church.name: Christ Church
shimla|Christ Church.title: Christ Church, Shimla

shimla|Himachal State Museum.extract:
The Himachal State Museum is a cultural museum located in Shimla, in the Indian Himalayan state of Himachal Pradesh.
The museum was established in 1974 in Inverarm, a house at the top of Inverarm Hill that during the British Raj was the hot season residence of Lord William Beresford (and frequently used for overflow guests at the Viceroy's house in Shimla, Peterhoff, which was smaller), and subsequently of Edwin Henry Hayter Collen and then Edward FitzGerald Law.
shimla|Himachal State Museum.name: Himachal State Museum
shimla|Himachal State Museum.title: Himachal State Museum

shimla|Jakhu Temple.extract: Jakhu Temple (also Jakhoo Temple) is an ancient Hindu temple in Shimla, Himachal Pradesh, India, dedicated to the Hindu deity Lord Hanuman. It is situated at Jakhu Hill, Shimla's highest peak, 2.5 km (1.6 mi) east of the Ridge at a height of 2,455 m (8,054 ft) above sea level.
shimla|Jakhu Temple.name: Jakhu Temple
shimla|Jakhu Temple.title: Jakhu Temple

shimla|Kufri.description: Hill Station in Himachal Pradesh, India
shimla|Kufri.extract: Kufri is a resort hill station in the district of Shimla, India. It is located 12 km (7.5 mi) from the state capital Shimla on the National Highway 5 (also known as Hindustan-Tibet road).
shimla|Kufri.name: Kufri
shimla|Kufri.title: Kufri, India

shimla|Lower Bazaar.description: Neighbourhood and Market in Shimla, Himachal Pradesh, India
shimla|Lower Bazaar.extract: Lower Bazaar is a market in Shimla city. It is just below the Middle Bazaar and Mall Road.
shimla|Lower Bazaar.name: Lower Bazaar
shimla|Lower Bazaar.title: Lower Bazaar, Shimla

shimla|Mall Road.description: Major hangout and shopping centre in Shimla
shimla|Mall Road.extract: Mall Road is one of the main financial, commercial and business centres in Shimla, the capital city of Himachal Pradesh, India. Constructed during British colonial rule, the Mall road is located a level below The Ridge.
shimla|Mall Road.name: Mall Road
shimla|Mall Road.title: Mall Road, Shimla

shimla|The Ridge.description: Pedestrian Avenue in Himachal Pradesh, India
shimla|The Ridge.extract: The Ridge road is a large open space, located in the center of Shimla, the capital city of Himachal Pradesh, India.  The Ridge is the hub of all cultural activities of Shimla.
shimla|The Ridge.name: The Ridge
shimla|The Ridge.title: The Ridge, Shimla

shimla|Viceregal Lodge (Rashtrapati Niwa.description: Former residence of the British Viceroy of India in Shimla, Himachal Pradesh
shimla|Viceregal Lodge (Rashtrapati Niwa.extract: The Rashtrapati Niwas (literally the "President's Residence"), formerly known as Viceregal Lodge, is located on the Observatory Hill in Boileauganj, Shimla, Himachal Pradesh, India. It was formerly the residence of the British Viceroy of India.
shimla|Viceregal Lodge (Rashtrapati Niwa.name: Viceregal Lodge (Rashtrapati Niwas)
shimla|Viceregal Lodge (Rashtrapati Niwa.title: Rashtrapati Niwas

shirdi|Shri Sai Baba Samadhi Mandir.extract: The Shri Saibaba Temple, Shirdi, also known as Shri Saibaba Samadhi Mandir, is a prominent Hindu temple complex located in Shirdi, Ahilyanagar district, Maharashtra, India. Dedicated to the 19th-century saint Sai Baba of Shirdi, it is one of the most visited pilgrimage sites in India, attracting millions of devotees annually from India and abroad.
shirdi|Shri Sai Baba Samadhi Mandir.name: Shri Sai Baba Samadhi Mandir
shirdi|Shri Sai Baba Samadhi Mandir.title: Shri Sai Baba Temple, Shirdi

srinagar|Dal Lake.extract: Dal (Urdu pronunciation: [ɖəl] ; Kashmiri pronunciation: [ɖal]) is a freshwater lake in Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir in Indian-administered Kashmir. It is an urban lake, the second largest lake in Jammu and Kashmir, and the most visited place in Srinagar by tourists and locals.
srinagar|Dal Lake.name: Dal Lake
srinagar|Dal Lake.title: Dal Lake

srinagar|Hazratbal Shrine.description: Muslim shrine in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, India
srinagar|Hazratbal Shrine.extract: The Hazratbal Shrine, also known as Dargah Hazratbal, is a Sufi dargah and mosque located in Hazratbal area of Srinagar, in the union territory of Jammu and Kashmir, India. The shrine houses the Moi-e-Muqqadas, a relic traditionally believed to be a hair strand of the Islamic Prophet Muhammad.
srinagar|Hazratbal Shrine.name: Hazratbal Shrine
srinagar|Hazratbal Shrine.title: Hazratbal Shrine

srinagar|Nishat Bagh.description: Terraced Mughal garden near Dal Lake, in Srinagar, Indian-administered Kashmir
srinagar|Nishat Bagh.extract: Nishat Bagh (lit. 'Garden of Joy' or 'Garden of Delight') is a terraced Mughal garden built on the eastern bank of the Dal Lake, close to Srinagar in the Indian-administered union territory of Jammu and Kashmir in the disputed Kashmir region. It is the second-largest Mughal garden in the Kashmir Valley after Shalimar Bagh.
srinagar|Nishat Bagh.name: Nishat Bagh
srinagar|Nishat Bagh.title: Nishat Bagh

srinagar|Old City (Downtown Srinagar).description: Place in Jammu and Kashmir, India
srinagar|Old City (Downtown Srinagar).extract: Downtown, popularly known as Shahar-e-Khaas, is the largest and the most densely populated area of the city of Srinagar in the union territory of Jammu and Kashmir, India. The area is mostly located on the banks of Jhelum River about five km (3.1 mi) from city center.
srinagar|Old City (Downtown Srinagar).name: Old City (Downtown Srinagar)
srinagar|Old City (Downtown Srinagar).title: Downtown, Srinagar

srinagar|Pari Mahal.extract: Pari Mahal (lit. 'palace of fairies') is a seven-terraced Mughal garden built on the top of the Zabarwan mountain range. It overlooks the city of Srinagar and the south-west of Dal Lake in the Indian union territory of Jammu and Kashmir.
srinagar|Pari Mahal.name: Pari Mahal
srinagar|Pari Mahal.title: Pari Mahal

srinagar|Shalimar Bagh (Mughal Gardens).description: Mughal garden at Dal Lake, Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir
srinagar|Shalimar Bagh (Mughal Gardens).extract: Shalimar Bagh (Urdu pronunciation: [ʃɑːliːmɑːr bɑːɣ] ; Kashmiri pronunciation: [ʃaːlɨməːr baːɣ]) is a Mughal garden in Srinagar, Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir, located at the northeast of Dal Lake. It is also known as Shalimar Garden, Farah Baksh, and Faiz Baksh.
srinagar|Shalimar Bagh (Mughal Gardens).name: Shalimar Bagh (Mughal Gardens)
srinagar|Shalimar Bagh (Mughal Gardens).title: Shalimar Bagh, Srinagar

srinagar|Shankaracharya Temple.extract: Shankaracharya Temple or Jyeshteshwara Temple is a Hindu temple situated on top of the Zabarwan Range in Srinagar in the Kashmir Valley of the union territory of Jammu and Kashmir, India. It is dedicated to Shiva.
srinagar|Shankaracharya Temple.name: Shankaracharya Temple
srinagar|Shankaracharya Temple.title: Shankaracharya Temple

tirupati|Govindaraja Swamy Temple.extract: Sri Govindarajaswamy Temple is an ancient Hindu Vaishnavite temple situated in the heart of Tirupati city in Tirupati district of Andhra Pradesh in India. The temple was built during 12th century and was consecrated in the year 1130 AD by Ramanuja as per the Vaikhanasa traditions, and the pancharatra jeeyar overseeing the divya prabandam recitation.
tirupati|Govindaraja Swamy Temple.name: Govindaraja Swamy Temple
tirupati|Govindaraja Swamy Temple.title: Govindaraja Temple, Tirupati

tirupati|Kapila Theertham.extract: Kapila Theertham is a small Shaivite temple and theertham, located at Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh, India. The idol of Shiva is believed to have been installed by Sage Kapila, so god Shiva here is referred to as Kapileswara.
tirupati|Kapila Theertham.name: Kapila Theertham
tirupati|Kapila Theertham.title: Kapila Theertham

tirupati|Talakona Waterfalls.extract: Talakona is situated in Tirupati district of Andhra Pradesh, India. It is a resort with waterfalls, dense forests and wildlife.
tirupati|Talakona Waterfalls.name: Talakona Waterfalls
tirupati|Talakona Waterfalls.title: Talakona

tirupati|Tirumala Venkateswara Temple.description: Hindu temple in Andhra Pradesh, India
tirupati|Tirumala Venkateswara Temple.extract: The Venkateswara Swami Temple—also known as Tirumala Temple, Tirupati Temple and Tirupati Balaji Temple—is a Hindu temple located in the hills of Tirumala, within Tirupati Urban Mandal, Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh, India. The temple is dedicated to Venkateswara, a form of Vishnu, who is believed to have appeared on earth to save mankind from trials and troubles of Kali Yuga.
tirupati|Tirumala Venkateswara Temple.name: Tirumala Venkateswara Temple
tirupati|Tirumala Venkateswara Temple.title: Venkateswara Temple, Tirumala

udaipur|City Palace.extract: City Palace (Raj Mahal), Udaipur is a palace complex situated in the city of Udaipur in the Indian state of Rajasthan. It was built over a period of nearly 400 years, with contributions from several rulers of the Mewar dynasty.
udaipur|City Palace.name: City Palace
udaipur|City Palace.title: City Palace, Udaipur

udaipur|Fateh Sagar Lake.extract: Fateh Sagar Lake is situated in the city of Udaipur in the Indian state of Rajasthan. It is an artificial lake named after Maharana Fateh Singh of Udaipur and Mewar, constructed north-west of Udaipur, to the north of Lake Pichola in the 1680s.
udaipur|Fateh Sagar Lake.name: Fateh Sagar Lake
udaipur|Fateh Sagar Lake.title: Fateh Sagar Lake

udaipur|Jag Mandir.extract: Jag Mandir is a palace built on an island in Lake Pichola. It is also called the "Lake Garden Palace".
udaipur|Jag Mandir.name: Jag Mandir
udaipur|Jag Mandir.title: Jag Mandir Palace

udaipur|Jagdish Temple.extract: Jagdish Temple is a large Hindu temple in the middle of Udaipur in Rajasthan, just outside the royal palace. It has been in continuous worship since 1651.
udaipur|Jagdish Temple.name: Jagdish Temple
udaipur|Jagdish Temple.title: Jagdish Temple, Udaipur

udaipur|Lake Palace.extract: Lake Palace (formerly known as Jag Niwas Palace) is a former summer palace of the royal dynasty of Mewar, now operated as a hotel. The Lake Palace is located on the island of Jag Niwas in Lake Pichola, Udaipur, India, and its natural foundation spans 4 acres (16,000 m2).
udaipur|Lake Palace.name: Lake Palace
udaipur|Lake Palace.title: Lake Palace

udaipur|Lake Pichola.extract: Lake Pichola, in Udaipur city in the Indian state of Rajasthan, is an artificial freshwater lake, created in the year 1362, named after the nearby Picholi village. It is one of the several contiguous lakes, and developed over the last few centuries in and around Udaipur city.
udaipur|Lake Pichola.name: Lake Pichola
udaipur|Lake Pichola.title: Lake Pichola

udaipur|Saheliyon-ki-Bari.extract:
Saheliyon-ki-Bari (Courtyard or Garden of the Maidens) is a major garden and a popular tourist space in Udaipur in the Indian state of Rajasthan.
It lies in the northern part of the city and has fountains and kiosks, a lotus pool and marble elephants.
udaipur|Saheliyon-ki-Bari.name: Saheliyon-ki-Bari
udaipur|Saheliyon-ki-Bari.title: Saheliyon-ki-Bari

udaipur|Sajjangarh (Monsoon Palace).description: Palatial hilltop residence in Udaipur, Rajasthan
udaipur|Sajjangarh (Monsoon Palace).extract: The Monsoon Palace, also known as the Sajjan Garh Palace, is a hilltop palatial residence in the city of Udaipur, Rajasthan in India, overlooking the Fateh Sagar Lake. It is named Sajjangarh after Maharana Sajjan Singh (1874–1884) of the Mewar dynasty, whom it was built for in 1884.
udaipur|Sajjangarh (Monsoon Palace).name: Sajjangarh (Monsoon Palace)
udaipur|Sajjangarh (Monsoon Palace).title: Monsoon Palace

ujjain|Kal Bhairav Temple.description: Hindu temple in Madhya Pradesh, India
ujjain|Kal Bhairav Temple.extract: Kal Bhairav temple is a Hindu temple located in the Ujjain city of Madhya Pradesh, India. It is dedicated to Kal Bhairav, the guardian deity of the city.
ujjain|Kal Bhairav Temple.name: Kal Bhairav Temple
ujjain|Kal Bhairav Temple.title: Kal Bhairav Temple, Ujjain

ujjain|Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga.extract: Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga (IAST: mahākāleśvara) is a Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva and is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, shrines which are said to be the most sacred abodes of Shiva. It is located in the ancient city of Ujjain in the state of Madhya Pradesh, India.
ujjain|Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga.name: Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga
ujjain|Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga.title: Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga

ujjain|Mangalnath Temple.description: Hindu temple in Madhya Pradesh, India
ujjain|Mangalnath Temple.extract: The Mangalnath Temple is a Hindu temple located in the Ujjain city of Madhya Pradesh. It is dedicated to Mahadeva, the guardian deity of the city.
ujjain|Mangalnath Temple.name: Mangalnath Temple
ujjain|Mangalnath Temple.title: Mangalnath Temple

ujjain|Vedh Shala (Jantar Mantar).extract: Jantar Mantar or Vedh Shala in New Ujjain is an observatory designed to be used with the naked eye. It is one of five Jantar Mantar in India.
ujjain|Vedh Shala (Jantar Mantar).name: Vedh Shala (Jantar Mantar)
ujjain|Vedh Shala (Jantar Mantar).title: Jantar Mantar, Ujjain

varanasi|Dalmandi.extract: Dalmandi (meaning Lentil Market), officially known as Hakim Mohammad Jafar Marg is one of the largest markets of Varanasi, spanning from Beniyabagh to Chowk Police Station near Kashi Vishwanath Temple. It is located in Purvanchal and is mostly run by Muslims.
varanasi|Dalmandi.name: Dalmandi
varanasi|Dalmandi.title: Dalmandi

vrindavan|Banke Bihari Temple.description: Hindu temple dedicated to the combined form of Radha Krishna in Vrindavan
vrindavan|Banke Bihari Temple.extract: Banke Bihari Temple is a Hindu temple situated in the town of Vrindavan, Mathura district of Uttar Pradesh, India. The temple is dedicated to Banke Bihari who is believed to be the combined form of Radha and Krishna.
vrindavan|Banke Bihari Temple.name: Banke Bihari Temple
vrindavan|Banke Bihari Temple.title: Banke Bihari Temple

vrindavan|Govardhan Hill.description: Sacred Hindu site in Uttar Pradesh, India
vrindavan|Govardhan Hill.extract: Govardhana Hill (Sanskrit: गोवर्धन; pronounced [ɡoːʋɐrdʰɐnɐ]), also called Mount Govardhana and Giriraj, is a sacred Hindu site in the Mathura district of Uttar Pradesh, India on an 8 km long hill located in the area of Govardhan and Radha Kund, which is about 21 kilometres (13 miles) from Vrindavan. It is the sacred centre of Braj and is identified as a natural form of Krishna, the Govardhana Shila.
vrindavan|Govardhan Hill.name: Govardhan Hill
vrindavan|Govardhan Hill.title: Govardhan Hill

vrindavan|ISKCON Temple Vrindavan.description: Radha Krishna Temple in Vrindavan, India
vrindavan|ISKCON Temple Vrindavan.extract: ISKCON Vrindavan,  also called Sri Krishna Balaram Mandir, is one of the major ISKCON temples in the world. It is a Gaudiya Vaishnava temple located in the city of Vrindavan, Mathura district, in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.
vrindavan|ISKCON Temple Vrindavan.name: ISKCON Temple Vrindavan
vrindavan|ISKCON Temple Vrindavan.title: ISKCON Temple, Vrindavan

vrindavan|Nidhivan.description: Sacred forest site dedicated to Radha and Krishna in Vrindavan, India
vrindavan|Nidhivan.extract: Nidhivan (Hindi: निधिवन meaning, Tulsi Forest) is one of the sacred sites of  Vrindavan, situated in the Mathura district, Uttar Pradesh, India. It is considered as the most prominent site dedicated to the pastimes of the Hindu deities Radha and Krishna and their cowherd companions, the Gopikas.
vrindavan|Nidhivan.name: Nidhivan
vrindavan|Nidhivan.title: Nidhivan, Vrindavan

vrindavan|Prem Mandir.description: Hindu temple dedicated to Radha Krishna and Sita Rama
vrindavan|Prem Mandir.extract: Prem Mandir is a Hindu temple in Vrindavan, Mathura district, Western Uttar Pradesh, India. The temple was established by Kripalu Maharaj.
vrindavan|Prem Mandir.name: Prem Mandir
vrindavan|Prem Mandir.title: Prem Mandir, Vrindavan

vrindavan|Radha Raman Temple.description: Hindu temple dedicated to combined form of Radha Krishna in Vrindavan
vrindavan|Radha Raman Temple.extract: Sri Radha Raman Temple, is a Hindu temple situated in Vrindavan, India. It is dedicated to Krishna who is worshiped as Radha Ramana.
vrindavan|Radha Raman Temple.name: Radha Raman Temple
vrindavan|Radha Raman Temple.title: Radha Raman Temple, Vrindavan

katra|Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra railw.query: Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra railway station
